Explain in your own words what 'Mercantile Trade and the Royal Charter of 1600' refers to.
questions.a: A commercial system where an enterprise secures exclusive trading privileges to purchase commodities at minimal rates and resell them in distant markets at substantial profit.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Mercantile Trade and the Royal Charter of 1600'.
questions.a: Monopoly charters eliminated domestic competition while driving armed rivalry against other European trading companies.

Explain in your own words what 'Establishment of Trade in Bengal and Farman Abuse' refers to.
questions.a: The expansion of British fortified settlements around Calcutta and the misuse of Mughal royal trade exemptions by Company servants for private enterprise.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Establishment of Trade in Bengal and Farman Abuse'.
questions.a: Private trade duty evasion severely depleted Bengal treasury revenues and caused sharp political friction with the Nawabs.

questions.a: The decisive confrontation in 1757 where the Company led by Robert Clive overthrew Nawab Sirajuddaulah through military action and internal conspiracy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Battle of Plassey (1757)'.
questions.a: Plassey marked the first major territorial and political triumph of the British in the Indian subcontinent.

Explain in your own words what 'Battle of Buxar and the Grant of Diwani (1765)' refers to.
questions.a: The formal transfer of fiscal administration rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the Company by the Mughal Emperor following the Battle of Buxar.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Battle of Buxar and the Grant of Diwani (1765)'.
questions.a: Assumption of Diwani allowed Bengal revenues to fund military conquests and trade purchases without importing bullion from Britain.

Explain in your own words what 'The System of Subsidiary Alliance' refers to.
questions.a: A treaty framework compelling native rulers to disband independent armies, house Company troops at local expense, and surrender territory if payments defaulted.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The System of Subsidiary Alliance'.
questions.a: Residents acted as virtual rulers within allied states while the alliance mechanism progressively annexed princely dominions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Anglo-Mysore Wars and Tipu Sultan'.

concepts.title: Policy of Paramountcy and Regional Resistance

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Policy of Paramountcy and Regional Resistance' refers to.
questions.a: The doctrine initiated under Lord Hastings asserting that British authority was supreme over all Indian states, justifying direct intervention and territorial seizure.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Policy of Paramountcy and Regional Resistance'.
questions.a: Paramountcy justified aggressive expansionism but sparked armed anti-colonial resistance across various local territories.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Policy of Paramountcy and Regional Resistance', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'The Doctrine of Lapse' refers to.
questions.a: An annexation policy introduced by Lord Dalhousie decreeing that any dependent princely state lacking a natural male heir would automatically lapse to British control.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Doctrine of Lapse'.
questions.a: The policy barred adopted heirs from inheriting sovereignty, leading to widespread dispossession of historic dynasties.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'The Doctrine of Lapse', in plain ASCII form.

Explain in your own words what 'Colonial Administrative and Judicial System' refers to.
questions.a: The administrative framework dividing British possessions into Presidencies and establishing dual district courts (civil and criminal) under European District Collectors.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Colonial Administrative and Judicial System'.
questions.a: Standardized digests of Hindu and Muslim laws centralized legal authority under British judicial oversight.

concepts.title: Structure and Evolution of the Sepoy Army

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Structure and Evolution of the Sepoy Army' refers to.
questions.a: The transformation of the British military apparatus from traditional cavalry-dominant units to disciplined, musket-bearing infantry recruited from local peasantries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Structure and Evolution of the Sepoy Army'.
questions.a: European military drill created professional discipline but disregarded deep-seated caste and religious identities of sepoys.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Structure and Evolution of the Sepoy Army', in plain ASCII form.
